amaarae.bio: Ghanaian-American singer, songwriter and producer Amaarae makes adventurous pop anchored by her distinctive high-register vocals and an unpredictable approach to production.

anaïs cardot.bio: Montréal singer-songwriter Anaïs Cardot makes intimate French-language soul and R&B, pairing warm vocals with emotionally direct writing.

anders.bio: Toronto singer and songwriter anders makes contemporary R&B with a moody, melodic sound closely associated with the city's late-night scene.

anna katarina.bio: Vancouver singer-songwriter and producer Anna Katarina makes melodic indie pop and rock shaped by folk and soul influences.

anna sofia.bio: Toronto singer-songwriter Anna Sofia emerged as a teenager with candid alternative-pop songs built around sharp hooks and diaristic writing.

anomalie.bio: Montréal keyboardist, composer and producer Nicolas Dupuis records as Anomalie, bringing jazz-fusion musicianship into groove-driven electronic production.

aqyila.bio: Toronto singer-songwriter Aqyila makes contemporary R&B and pop with confessional writing and a soulful vocal style.

ardn.bio: Ugandan-Canadian rapper ARDN is based in Edmonton, where he has built an independent career around introspective, melodic hip-hop.

ariel posen.bio: Winnipeg singer-songwriter, guitarist and producer Ariel Posen pairs detailed songwriting with the guitar work that has earned him an international following.

arman ayva.bio: Montréal-based composer and producer Arman Ayva makes instrumental jazz-fusion with electronic textures and a strong jazz-funk foundation.

ashton adams.bio: Canadian DJ and producer Ashton Adams makes bass-heavy electronic music and club records, with production work that also reaches into hip-hop.

beatchild.bio: Toronto producer, songwriter and multi-instrumentalist Beatchild, also known as Slakah the Beatchild, has built a wide-ranging catalogue rooted in hip-hop, R&B and soul.

bobby bazini.bio: Québec singer-songwriter Bobby Bazini, from the Upper Laurentians, is known for warm vocals and guitar-led songs rooted in soul, blues and folk.

birthday boy.bio: Toronto producer, DJ and musician Birthday Boy, born Eoin, makes sample-minded production shaped by the city's hip-hop and club scenes.

love inc..bio:
Toronto dance group Love Inc. brought together DJ and producer Chris Sheppard, producer Brad Daymond and vocalist Simone Denny during a period when Canadian club music was breaking into mainstream pop. Their 1998 self-titled debut produced the hits "Broken Bones" and "You're a Superstar," with the latter later reaching the UK Top 10. The album went platinum in Canada, while "Broken Bones" won the 1999 JUNO Award for Best Dance Recording.

After Daymond's departure, Sheppard and Denny continued with the 2000 album Into the Night. Love Inc.'s short catalogue remains closely tied to the late-1990s Canadian dance boom, when house and Eurodance regularly crossed from clubs and MuchMusic into national pop culture.

dubmatique.bio:
Montréal's Dubmatique helped move francophone hip-hop from an emerging underground scene into Québec's mainstream. The group's 1997 debut La force de comprendre reached platinum status, while songs including "Soul pleureur" brought French-language rap to a much wider audience.

Their breakthrough arrived before Québec's major awards system even had a dedicated hip-hop album category: La force de comprendre won the Félix for Alternative Rock Album of the Year in 1997, and Dubmatique won Group of the Year the following year. In 2019, SOCAN recognized "Soul pleureur" as the first Québec hip-hop song to receive a SOCAN Classic Award. The group's commercial success helped establish a path for later generations of francophone Canadian rappers.
